studies.title: Better Than A Thousand Months
studies.meaning: The pronoun in the first line has nothing before it in the surah, and the commentators agree it means the Quran. It came down on a night the surah names but does not date. Then comes the question form, which the Quran uses to say a thing is past describing. The comparison given is arithmetic and strange: better than a thousand months. Angels come down with every command, and the night is called peace until dawn rather than said to hold peace.
studies.historicalContext: Meccan by the tradition this collection follows, though some authorities place it in Medina. No set occasion is reported. Other passages tie the night it describes to the month of fasting. The sources record several views about which night of that month is meant. They generally point at the last ten, and at the odd-numbered ones, without settling on a date.

keyTerms.note: The root covers determining an amount, having power, and being of value. All three readings are recorded: the night on which things are apportioned, the night of power, and the night of great worth.
A form implying descent in stages or repeatedly rather than in one movement. Used with a present-tense verb, it describes the night as something that happens rather than something that happened once.

The word for peace is placed first and the night second, so the sentence identifies the night with peace rather than describing it as peaceful. Arabic word order carries the emphasis the English has to spell out.

studies.lifeInProphetsTime: A thousand months is about eighty-three years. That was more than a full lifetime in seventh-century Arabia. The comparison is not an idea. It offers a person more than his whole life in the space of one night. For an audience that counted wealth in seasons and life in a few decades, that is the largest exchange rate anyone had heard proposed.
studies.didYouKnow: The phrase naming the night occurs three times in five short lines, which in a surah this length is an unusual density. Nothing else in the chapter is repeated. The effect is that the name arrives, is questioned, and is answered, and by the fourth ayah the surah can stop naming it and simply say what happens in it.
studies.theologicalSignificance: Time is described as unequal, which is a specific claim. One night is said to carry more than eighty years. So the value of a period is not a matter of its length. That has a consequence for how a person thinks about a life. What is decisive may take up very little of it. The night is also left undated, which keeps the search open and makes the last third of a month a stretch of attention rather than a single appointment.

crossReferences.why: Names the month this night belongs to, and connects the descent of the Quran to the same period.
Describes the same night with a different phrase, adding that every decided matter is separated out in it.
Contains the lines that came down on the night this surah describes, according to the classical accounts.

studies.applyIt: Give one night this year the shape this surah describes: no screen, no plans, a few hours awake with something worth saying. It does not have to be the right night, and nobody knows which that is. The practice the surah produces is looking for it, and looking has to be done on ordinary nights.
studies.explainEasier: God sent the Quran down on the Night of Decree. That one night is worth more than a thousand months. Angels and the Spirit come down in it with every order from God. It is peace, all the way until dawn.
